The EFIE formulation leads to dense, complex, and often ill-conditioned linear systems.
The condition number of EFIE matrices grows approximately as the square root of the scatterer size in wavelengths and linearly with discretization density.
Direct solvers require O(n^2) storage and O(n^3) operations, becoming impractical for large problems.
Krylov iterative methods without preconditioning scale as O(n^0.5) in iteration count for EFIE.
The SPAI preconditioner is computed by minimizing the Frobenius norm of I - AM under sparsity constraints.
The sparsity pattern for SPAI is chosen based on mesh box partitioning and nearest neighbor edges.
SPAI construction reduces to solving n independent least-squares problems, enabling high parallelism.
MLFMA is used to accelerate matrix-vector products in large-scale scattering problems.
Numerical tests show SPAI reduces GMRES iterations significantly compared to no preconditioner or diagonal scaling.
On a cylinder problem (n=1299), SPAI reduced GMRES(80) iterations to 70 compared to 454 for ILU(0).
For large aircraft problems with over 1 million unknowns, full GMRES without preconditioning often fails to converge within practical time or memory limits.
Spectral deflation shifts small eigenvalues of the preconditioned matrix to improve convergence robustness.
Eigenpairs for spectral deflation are computed using ARPACK's IRA method before the iterative solve.
Parallel scalability tests show preconditioner construction and application times remain nearly constant per processor as problem size grows.
CFIE systems require significantly fewer iterations than EFIE, e.g., 22 iterations for preconditioned GMRES on a 213,084 DOF aircraft problem.
The paper uses Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions for discretizing surface currents.
The preconditioner density decreases as problem size increases due to fixed unknowns per box in the mesh partitioning.
Restarted GMRES with large restart values reduces memory but can deteriorate convergence rates.
The preconditioner is less prone to instabilities than incomplete LU factorizations on EFIE systems.
Numerical experiments were performed on a Compaq Alpha cluster with up to 64 processors.
